A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COCO-FACET benchmark and promptable-image-embedding methods. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval evaluations, prompt comparisons, acceleration experiments and failure-case analyses, including five-run results with standard errors.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds comparator evaluations, sensitivity and robustness experiments, resource measurements and gradient visualizations.

M1.justification: Prompt generation, conditional image embeddings, prompt selection and the W=BA^T approximation applied through the query remain unchanged. v2 documents category-specific sampling more explicitly but introduces no new proposed algorithm component.

E1.justification: MSCOCO, COCO-FACET, Place365 and SUN397 coverage is retained. Appendix E.2 adds inference scenarios restricting stored prompts to other attributes or drawing approximation samples from another attribute-category pool, modestly extending the tested availability conditions.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix C.2/Table 14 newly evaluates FLAIR, previously only discussed, with CLIP-ViT-B/16 as a size-matched control. The original retrievers and text-based comparison remain; CLOC is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation design with K=5–100 sweeps, K=10 timing on duplicated pools up to 20 million images with GPU or CPU search, restricted four-prompt sets, and K=100 sampling from another category. Original benchmark construction and retrieval metrics remain unchanged; the more explicit sampling description does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond retained prompt-wording checks and failure cases, v2 adds sample-size sensitivity (Figure 3), gradient saliency analysis (Figure 4), computational scaling measurements (Appendix C.3), and disjoint-prompt and cross-category sampling tests (Appendix E.2). These substantially broaden investigation of efficiency, mechanisms and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Five independent runs and standard errors were already reported in v1 Appendix C.3/Table 14 and are retained in v2 Table 15. The new K sweep and disjoint-sample experiment also use five-run averaging; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Matched original numerical results are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results. Table 14 reports average Recall@1/Recall@5 of 33.0/50.3 for FLAIR versus 35.0/49.8 for CLIP-ViT-B/16; Table 19 reports 61.4 average Recall@5 with cross-category samples versus 67.0 with default sampling. New sensitivity, timing, memory, saliency and disjoint-prompt outcomes supplement these; they are additional conditions, not revised same-setting performance.

T1.justification: The approximation equations, transpose identity, normalization discussion and symbolic embedding-cost expressions are retained. The sampling qualification concerns experimental applicability; no new mathematical derivation, formal result or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the benchmark, retriever limitations, promptable embeddings and two acceleration strategies. The same 15% and 8% headline Recall@5 improvements and generalization claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges that acceleration is not entirely zero-shot and depends on query-category information, with reduced reliability when suitable prompts or same-category samples are unavailable. It also adds interpretations of approximation failures, computational bottlenecks, gradient visualizations and the advantages of flexible MLLM image focus. These materially expand v1's limitations and mechanism discussion.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the Dropbox benchmark pointer with a GitHub repository link and clarifies the approximation sampling pool. It adds FAISS IndexFlatIP, batch-size and memory information, duplicated-pool timing procedures, and crop-weighting details for the gradient visualizations. Existing model, hardware and prompt documentation is retained.

R1.justification: The cited works remain the same, but v2 adds an explicit distinction from MMVP-VLM in Section 3 and expands comparison with CLOC and FLAIR in Appendix C.2. This sharpens positioning around retrieval-pool size and flexible image focus without substantially changing the research framing.

P1.justification: Most original prose and section order remain. v2 makes localized wording edits, switches to author-year citations, adds acknowledgments, expands Appendix C and divides limitations into benchmark and method subsections. This is targeted editing and organization rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds an eight-panel sensitivity figure, a three-panel saliency figure, and tables for FLAIR, runtime and disjoint conditions. Existing displays are also reflowed or lightly adjusted. v1's standard-error Table 14 becomes Table 15, and its example Figures 3–4 become Figures 5–6; these are retained content.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the acceleration claims more assessable through sensitivity tests, measured resource costs and explicit tests of dependence on category information. The FLAIR comparison and implementation disclosures provide additional support. These are useful targeted gains, while the central benchmark evidence remains unchanged and the large-pool timing results are limited to duplicated images.
